text:
Same model. Same prompt. Same DGX Spark.

The only thing that changed was how much thinking Qwen3.8-27B was allowed to use.

On one DGX Spark, with no output token cap:

Low reasoning:
5,364 tokens in 3m20s

Medium:
7,418 tokens in 5m06s

XHigh:
49,028 tokens in 37m24s

The reasoning traces went from roughly 4.5K characters to 11.4K, then all the way to 120K.

But the surprising part isn’t the extra 34 minutes.

The model didn’t simply spend longer polishing the same answer.

It produced three completely different water simulations.

Same model.
Same instructions.
Different reasoning budget.
Different approach to the problem.

That’s an important detail about reasoning models that gets lost when we only compare benchmark scores.

More compute at inference time can change the actual path the model takes.

Low reasoning can be enough when the task is straightforward.

Medium gives it more room to explore.

XHigh gives it enough budget to rethink the problem much more deeply, test different approaches internally, and eventually arrive at a substantially different implementation.

Of course, more thinking isn’t automatically better. If a task doesn’t benefit from deeper reasoning, burning 49K tokens and 37 minutes is just expensive overkill.

Insiden ini terjadi usai mereka mengkonsumsi Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG)...

Di sisi lain, pelaksanaan SOP dalam pengolahan dan distribusi MBG akan dievaluasi untuk mengetahui ada tidaknya kelalaian...

Sementara itu, Kepala SMAN 1 Lasem, Juhartutik, menyebut gejala pencernaan ini mulai terdeteksi secara masif pada Kamis (3/9/2026) pagi saat para siswa mulai masuk kelas...

"Tadi pagi anak-anak masuk, ada yang bilang 'Pak, saya diare'. Begitu guru mendata di masing-masing kelas, dalam beberapa menit langsung masuk laporan ada 777 orang (total guru dan siswa) yang diare," kata Juhartutik saat dimintai konfirmasi, Kamis (3/9/2026)...

Menu MBG untuk makan siang itu terdiri dari nasi, ayam bakar grill, tempe, lalapan, sambal teri goreng, serta buah semangka potong...

Sejumlah murid melaporkan ada kejanggalan pada buah pencuci mulut yang mereka santap karena terasa kecut...

Within an hour of Cursor Projects shipping, my feed was already split: "Should I use Cursor Projects or Bot?" Kent Dodds is keeping Bot. Others are moving to Projects.

I keep seeing this every time a new persistent coding agent interface ships. Claude Code added auto-mode. Cursor added the coordinator. Codex runs in Cloudflare now. Each has a different execution model, permission boundary, and strength profile.

My read: the next year of developer tooling is going to produce a dozen more of these, all with legitimate tradeoffs, none of them compatible with each other's context. Different tasks want different backends. Cursor Projects' coordinator delegating to parallel subagents is right for large refactors. Claude Code's direct loop is right for tight feedback cycles. Codex with Cloudflare isolation is right when you need auditability.

The gap is that there's no good way to run them together. Campfire is the open-source answer.

Run Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Goose, Aider, OpenHands, and more side by side in a single browser tab. Agent races: same task across multiple backends in isolated git worktrees, see which finishes first. Permission voting: majority-rules approves, any-deny blocks. Session replay. Cost dashboard. Shared semantic memory across agents.

You don't have to pick one coding agent.

text:
Di tengah sorotan publik terhadap kasus keracunan massal yang diduga berasal dari program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), ketegasan aparat penegak hukum mulai dipertanyakan. 

Pakar hukum pidana dari Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta (UMY), Trisno Raharjo, menilai Polri belum menunjukkan keseriusan dalam mengusut tuntas peristiwa tersebut.

Menurut Trisno, keracunan massal bukanlah delik aduan. Polisi seharusnya bertindak cepat dengan langsung melakukan penyelidikan dan penyidikan tanpa perlu menunggu adanya laporan resmi dari pihak korban.

"Maka saya bilang ndak perlu itu dilaporkan dan itu bukan delik aduan," ujar Trisno saat dihubungi, Jumat (11/9/2026).

Isu keterlibatan institusi kepolisian dalam penyediaan program MBG disinyalir menjadi batu sandungan. Diketahui, kepolisian menjadi salah satu pengelola Satuan Pelayanan Pemenuhan Gizi (SPPG) atau dapur MBG terbanyak. 

Kondisi ini dikhawatirkan memicu potensi konflik kepentingan yang membuat proses hukum berjalan di tempat.

"Nah, kalau sudah seperti itu menjadikan pihak kepolisian itu tidak melaksanakan tugasnya dengan sungguh-sungguh. Jadi dia punya conflict of interest," tegasnya.

Ia menambahkan, keterlibatan kepolisian dalam pengelolaan dapur MBG tidak boleh melunturkan asas profesionalisme penegakan hukum. 

"Apalagi ternyata di belakang kita ketahui polisi paling banyak itu dapurnya. Tapi kan bukan masalah dia punya dapur atau tidak. Dia punya dapur pun, tugas penyidik itu harus profesional," lanjut Trisno.

Secara konklusif, Trisno mendesak Polri untuk membuka penyelidikan secara menyeluruh dan transparan terhadap seluruh dapur SPPG yang terindikasi bermasalah tanpa memandang bulu. 

Penanganan yang lambat atau terkesan membiarkan hanya akan memperburuk citra penegakan hukum di mata publik.

"Buka itu mana SPPG yang bermasalah, dan seterusnya. Kalau ndak terlibat pihak kepolisiannya, itu namanya tutup mata itu terhadap peristiwa yang luar biasa seperti ini," pungkasnya.

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 shipped 48 hours apart and both landed at exactly $10/$50 per million tokens, double what their predecessors cost in July. Kimi K3, out since mid-July, is still sitting at $3/$15. Two months ago the spread between the priciest and cheapest frontier model was 1.8x. It's now 6x, and nobody's context window even got bigger to justify it, Astra and K3 are both capped at roughly 1.05 million tokens.

Here's the number that never made it into a single launch post: Astra takes 322 seconds to produce its first token in reasoning mode, versus 55 for K3. That's not a chat model anymore, that's five minutes and twenty-two seconds of staring at a cursor before it says a word, and it changes the entire feel of an agent loop from "iterate quickly" to "go do something else and come back."

Astra genuinely is the better model, #1 in the world at reasoning, ranking #2 of 231 tracked models overall. But on coding and knowledge, the two categories most people actually live in day to day, K3 scores higher, while costing 233% less per task. Even after stacking a 70% cache hit rate, the gap barely moves, because output tokens never cache and both new flagships charge $50 against K3's $15.

The one thing neither new flagship has: K3's weights are published, all 1.4 terabytes of them, on Hugging Face. Nobody's actually running that at home, but it buys something narrower and more real, the price can't be changed on a version you've already downloaded. Two labs just repriced their flagships upward within 48 hours of each other, and everyone still on those endpoints absorbed it without a choice.

Running several coding agents gets messy fast. Garcon keeps the loop in one browser workspace.

Garcon is a self-hosted workspace for developers who want to run coding agents alongside the code on their own machine.

It helps you keep parallel work moving by putting agent chats, terminals, files, Git, and pull-request controls together, while letting you redirect active work instead of waiting for a run to finish.

Key features:

• Multi-window workspace – tile up to four resizable windows and keep task-specific tabs local to each one
• Agent choice – run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, OpenCode, Amp, Factory Droid, and Pi side by side
• In-flight steering – queue instructions, interrupt or redirect a turn, approve tool use, and pause or stop work in place
• Git review tools – inspect diffs and stage individual lines, hunks, files, or folders before committing
• Visible coordination – send provenance-labeled messages between chats and trace delegation lineage in Chat Map

It’s open-source (GPL-3.0 license).

Ratusan santri Pondok Pesantren Manbaul Hikam, Sidoarjo, diduga mengalami keracunan setelah menyantap makanan yang diduga berasal dari program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), Selasa (1/9) malam.

Satu per satu ambulans membawa para santri ke RSUD RT Notopuro, Sidoarjo. Sejumlah keluhan yang dilaporkan antara lain mual, sesak napas hingga kejang.

Informasi awal menyebut para santri menyantap makan siang sekitar pukul 13.00 WIB. Salah seorang santri bahkan menyebut hampir 90 persen siswa mengalami keluhan setelah menyantap jatah MBG.

Sejumlah pejabat, termasuk Bupati Sidoarjo, Dandim 0816/Sidoarjo, dan jajaran kepolisian, turut memantau proses penanganan.

Hingga kini, belum ada keterangan resmi mengenai jumlah pasti korban maupun penyebab kejadian. Pendataan dan pemeriksaan masih dilakukan petugas.

Kasus ini pun menambah sorotan terhadap pelaksanaan program MBG, terutama soal keamanan dan kualitas makanan yang diterima para penerima manfaat.

PWI Pusat Minta Klarifikasi atas Pencabutan Kartu Liputan Wartawan CNN Indonesia

Jakarta – Persatuan Wartawan Indonesia (PWI) Pusat menyampaikan keprihatinan atas pencabutan kartu liputan Istana yang dialami wartawan CNN Indonesia usai melontarkan pertanyaan mengenai program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) kepada Presiden Prabowo Subianto, Sabtu (27/9).

Ketua Umum PWI Pusat, Akhmad Munir, menegaskan bahwa tindakan tersebut berpotensi menghambat kemerdekaan pers dan bertentangan dengan amanat konstitusi serta Undang-Undang Nomor 40 Tahun 1999 tentang Pers.

“Pasal 28F UUD 1945 menjamin hak setiap orang untuk berkomunikasi dan memperoleh informasi. Sedangkan Pasal 4 UU Pers menegaskan kemerdekaan pers dijamin sebagai hak asasi warga negara, tanpa penyensoran atau pelarangan penyiaran,” ujar Munir dalam keterangan resmi, Minggu (28/9).

Munir juga mengingatkan bahwa Pasal 18 ayat (1) UU Pers menyebutkan setiap pihak yang dengan sengaja menghalangi atau menghambat pelaksanaan kemerdekaan pers dapat dikenai pidana penjara hingga dua tahun atau denda maksimal Rp500 juta.

Menurut Munir, pencabutan kartu liputan wartawan CNN Indonesia dengan alasan pertanyaan di luar agenda Presiden tidak dapat dibenarkan karena menghalangi tugas jurnalistik serta membatasi hak publik untuk memperoleh informasi.

Munir juga mendorong Biro Pers, Media, dan Informasi Sekretariat Presiden untuk segera memberikan klarifikasi resmi serta membuka ruang dialog dengan insan pers.

“Menjaga kemerdekaan pers berarti menjaga demokrasi. Oleh karena itu, setiap bentuk pembatasan yang bertentangan dengan konstitusi dan UU Pers harus dihentikan,” tegas Munir.

Giving an AI agent a production credential shouldn’t mean giving it the keys.

Warden is a secure gateway for connecting AI agents to enterprise systems such as MCP servers, cloud services, code hosts, observability tools, databases, and SaaS.

It helps you put identity, policy, and audit in the request path: the agent presents its identity, Warden evaluates the request, injects the upstream credential, and proxies the response.

Key features:

• Identity-based access – supports JWTs, TLS client certificates, SPIFFE SVIDs, and Kubernetes service-account tokens
• Per-request policy – evaluates access when each call happens, including MCP tool calls and arguments
• Credential isolation – agents can work without holding upstream secrets in their environment
• Broad provider coverage – fronts MCP, LLM, cloud, code-hosting, observability, ITSM, Kubernetes, secrets, and database systems
• Audit and attribution – records the identity, role, policy decision, and upstream for each request

It’s open-source (Mozilla Public License 2.0 license).

Instead of a new chat thread for every task, you get a single coordinator agent that stays alive, spawns subagents for parallel work, and never touches the code itself so it stays responsive. A Project runs on its own computer so closing your laptop doesn't stop it.

The meaningful difference in Cursor Projects: the coordinator never edits files, it only delegates. That keeps it responsive at the reasoning layer while subagents run concurrently.

Cursor shipped this as its first major architectural release since the SpaceX acquisition closed August 14. The persistent coordinator model is what engineering at scale actually requires.

Biro Pers, Media, dan Informasi (BPMI) Sekretariat Presiden akhirnya mengembalikan kartu identitas liputan istana milik jurnalis CNN Indonesia, Diana Valencia, yang sebelumnya sempat dicabut. Peristiwa pencabutan ini terjadi setelah Diana menanyakan Presiden Prabowo Subianto mengenai program MBG ketika presiden baru saja kembali dari lawatan luar negeri di Bandara Halim, Sabtu (27/9/2025).

Dalam wawancara khusus bersama Radio Elshinta, Pemimpin Redaksi CNN Indonesia, Titin Rosmasari, menjelaskan pihaknya langsung mengirim surat resmi ke BPMI yang ditembuskan kepada Menteri Sekretaris Negara dan Dewan Pers. Surat tersebut mempertanyakan alasan pencabutan ID pers Diana. “Kami mengirim surat resmi kemarin, pagi kami putuskan untuk mengirim secara daring, fisiknya kami sampaikan siang. Respon cepat zwkami terima, dan pagi ini kami bisa bertemu dengan Deputi II Protokol Pak Yusuf Permana serta Kepala Biro Pers, Media dan Informasi (BPMI), Ibu Erlin Suastini,” kata Titin.

Dalam pertemuan yang juga dihadiri Direktur CNN Indonesia Desi Anwar, Wakil Pemimpin Redaksi Revolusi Riza Zulverdi, perwakilan Dewan Pers Totok Suryanto, serta jurnalis Diana Valencia, BPMI mengakui adanya kekeliruan. Menurut Titin, Yusuf Permana menyatakan pencabutan itu diputuskan secara pribadi oleh Kepala Biro Pers Erlin Suastini. “Ada permintaan maaf kepada Diana yang disampaikan langsung oleh Bu Erlin. Beliau mengakui keputusannya dilakukan karena cukup emosi, seharian berada di Halim, dan merasa pertanyaan yang diajukan di luar konteks doorstop,” jelas Titin.

Erlin menugaskan timnya untuk mengambil ID liputan Diana setelah pertanyaan soal MBG diajukan. Namun, BPMI menegaskan bahwa yang dicabut adalah akses peliputan di istana, bukan identitas profesi jurnalis. Setelah klarifikasi, ID tersebut dikembalikan sehingga Diana kembali bisa bertugas meliput kegiatan di Istana kepresidenan.

Titin menyebut pencabutan ini sempat menekan psikologis Diana serta menimbulkan kebingungan bagi CNN dan komunitas pers. “Sepanjang saya berkarir di media, belum pernah ada pencabutan ID pers wartawan istana. Sangat mengejutkan bagi kami, dan ini juga menjadi pertanyaan publik serta komunitas pers pun mengecam peristiwa ini,” ungkapnya.

Deputi bidang Protokol, Yusuf Permana memastikan kejadian serupa tidak akan terulang. BPMI ditegaskan harus menjunjung tinggi kebebasan pers sebagaimana diatur dalam UU Nomor 40 Tahun 1999 dan menghormati pers sebagai pilar keempat demokrasi. “Deputi menyampaikan komitmen agar BPMI menghormati kerja pers yang kritis, profesional, dan fleksibel,” ujar Titin.

Ia menegaskan, langkah klarifikasi, pengembalian ID, dan permintaan maaf ini menjadi pelajaran penting bagi semua pihak. “Ini penting untuk menunjukkan secara langsung kepada teman-teman pers bahwa kebebasan pers tetap harus dihormati. Kami berharap ke depan tidak ada lagi kesan represif terhadap wartawan,” pungkasnya. (Nes)

Motor listrik buat antar nasi bungkus, tapi harganya bikin kantong negara ‘mark-up’ ke angkasa. Efisiensi anggaran katanya, tapi kok malah bikin Kejagung sibuk?

Stop losing coding-agent context every time you switch tools.

Claudexor is a local-first control plane for developers using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, OpenCode, and Antigravity CLI.

It helps you run coding work through one typed interface by keeping turns, patches, quota state, and execution evidence in a local workflow.

Key features:

• Multi-harness interface – runs supported coding CLIs behind one control plane instead of separate tool-specific flows
• Native session continuity – read-only questions can resume the vendor’s own native session
• Inspectable patches – write turns land as patches you can review before applying
• Cross-model review – best-of-N races can use independent reviewers and arbitration
• Account and quota handling – credential profiles sit side by side, with quota-aware routing where a vendor usage source exists

It’s open-source (MIT license).

text:
A terminal multiplexer for AI coding agents just raised $6M. Bessemer led it. YC and E2 participated. Tobi Lutke, Dane Knecht from Cloudflare, and Gorkem Yurtseven from https://t.co/wgZmOqI59X came in as angels.

Herdr is open source, built in Rust, and does one thing well: every agent gets a real terminal session with persistent state. Work survives disconnects. Multiple agents become an attention queue rather than a pile of windows.

Ian Nuttall built a full site in 12 hours yesterday using it. The orchestration pattern he described: Fable 5.1 as the lead, Astra high for research and data gathering, Astra low for backend implementation, Fable 5.1 low for design. All running in parallel.

What I keep noticing in that setup: the model tier mapping is explicit. Research tasks need reasoning quality. Backend implementation needs speed and volume. Design iteration is somewhere between. You don't use the same model everywhere, you use the right tier at each step.

This is the same layering pattern DevOps went through with compute: different instance types for different workloads. The teams building agent infrastructure today are building the scheduler, not the model.

Bessemer has invested in LinkedIn, Shopify, and Twilio early. Their bet here is on the orchestration layer, not the model layer. That framing matters.

text:
People are underestimating Grok

Myself included. But the progress week after week is becoming undeniable. 

Grok is nowhere close to being #1 yet. Claude is better at copy/design, Codex is great for coding, Grok is average at most things but the smaller things it does well, make it great. 

Pretty pumped what XAi builds when it gets the Cursor <> Grok merger done properly and when it cleans up its UI / interfaces for users + reaches Fable level comfort.

I have had a lot of pain points. don't get me wrong. This is far from perfect. Quotas burn during setup, routines miss their automation windows, and I still bounce between Grok, Cursor, and GrokBot usage limits because I still can't link the thing...but whatever. But I do see the puzzle coming together.

I currently have subscriptions to Claude, Cursor, Grok and Codex. I pray that Claude and Grok become one. I will probably drop Claude after I close some remaining work and keep OpenAI as an agent to loop against. Then start using some other open source models (lazy right now)

But let me purely talk about Grok.

Before, I had to use Claude Code which then sent items to Github. Then I needed separate items for Render / Supabase or whatever webhosting, and domain to get started.

Today, I can get stuff deployed via Grok Build and pushed to Github after so my other instances can also work on it the same time.

Grok Bot is the always-on teammate. And its now on https://t.co/0ib3oTvVok (still not in the CLI version...) and tt has its own cloud computer meaning browser, filesystem, terminal, logins. It keeps working when I close the laptop. And this week I lost my internet a few times and the work didn't die. I assign it tasks, it makes a squad and keeps pushing updates to my phone and Github. Its frickin amazing. Cron jobs without the hassle. 

Grok Build is the CLI when I need the other perks and am lazy, Still use CLI but really enjoying Build. Plan mode first so it does not touch files until I like the plan, parallel subagents in their own git worktrees. It stages, commits, pushes, opens branches. And it seems to run longer than when I use Fable where I hit limits in 20 minutes. 

On the brightside, I can get Fable to build the plan and review; and then bring that to Grok to actually do it with less hassle. This is where I hope Grok 4.7 or 5 can get to Fable's soft value and "smartness" so I don't need both.

Codex stays in the loop as the guy who hates my code. Right now I manual run or assign it tasks via Fable, and all three work in unison. I still haven't unlocked Cursor but saw some headlines where ideally it becomes the area where all tools work in unison, minus OpenAI killing access soon, so not great. 

Anyways long story short, Build gets me to build main, push to github and publish a site without having to visit mulitple sites. Its awesome for ideating and prototyping. And Grok Bots are cheap enough to run where you don't need insane credits to work on smaller things.

The vertical integration is making it where I barely need to leave my CLI and my browsers.

Mind you, I am not a coder. Last time I tried was in 2013 trying to pass Java and Data Tree class to get my Math/CompSci minor. Otherwise a finance dude who knows business requirements and works in excel spreadsheets.

So I am just amazed that I can prototype an idea that goes more niche on a weekend while feeling smart because i build a pseduo intelligent system (bet it has many problems) 

anyways a month ago i didn't know what a branch, tree, pull, render or supabase were, not really. its been fun.

build some weird stuff with whatever tool you like. niche stuff is best. i have market updates with grok now. 

also check out this: https://t.co/2TctHkQdoU

needs to be refreshed but thats two months worth of work. let me know what you think. will get it properly hosted when i work out the kinks.

Gue baru sadar hubungan 4 tahun gue harus selesai pas gue terbaring di IGD karena kolaps kerjaan, dan cowok gue cuma ngechat: 'Yang, makan siang aku gimana? Aku bingung cara redeem voucher GoFood yang di akun kamu.' Jam 2 siang, infus masih menggantung, dada gue sesek, dan di saat fisik gue remuk total, fokus utama laki-laki yang udah 4 tahun nemenin gue cuma seputar perutnya sendiri.

Sebagai anak sulung umur 27 tahun yang kerja jadi Senior Marketing Executive di Jakarta, gue terbiasa jadi 'penyelamat'. Nanggung bayaran kuliah adik, kelarin revisi deck jam 2 pagi, sampai ngurusin hal sepele cowok gue—mulai dari bayar listrik kosannya sampai urusan laundry. Gue selalu merasa, untuk bisa dicintai dan dihargai, gue harus terbukti 'berguna' dulu buat semua orang.

Tapi hari itu bener-bener puncaknya. Badan gue gemeteran, vonis dokter bilang gue burnout parah plus asam lambung kronis. Bukannya nanya keadaan gue gimana atau mau nyamperin ke rumah sakit, dia malah minta ditransfer uang kopi karena 'males top up e-wallet sendiri'. Di ranjang IGD yang dingin itu, kepala gue rasanya ditampar kenyataan paling pahit seumur hidup.

Selama 4 tahun ini, gue kira dia manja karena sayang. Ternyata itu weaponized incompetence—dia sengaja berpura-pura nggak bisa dan nggak paham biar gue yang ngerjain semuanya. Dan bodohnya, luka keberhargaan diri gue merespons itu sebagai bentuk kebutuhan. Gue ngerasa dibutuhkan, padahal gue cuma lagi dimanfaatin sama orang yang enggan bertumbuh dewasa.

Sambil nahan perih bekas jarum infus, jari gue gemeteran ngetik balasan: 'Login sendiri. Dan mulai hari ini, belajar ngurus hidup kamu sendiri. Kita selesai.' Dia langsung berondong telfon puluhan kali, panik—bukan karena takut kehilangan gue, tapi karena kehilangan fasilitas gratis yang selama ini gue sediakan atas nama 'cinta'.

Malam itu gue pulang naik Grab sendirian, bawa kantong obat yang berat. Tapi herannya, dada gue rasanya jauh lebih lapang dari biasanya. Gue baru sadar, kita nggak perlu terus-menerus terbukti berguna hanya untuk layak dicintai. Melepaskan orang yang sengaja bertindak tidak berdaya ternyata adalah bentuk tertinggi dari mencintai diri sendiri.

Sebuah Harapan Berbunga Layu

Seperti biasa, sore ini perutku sudah memberikan sinyal protes sejak tadi siang, menuntut untuk segera diisi. Aku pun segera naik motor untuk membelah kemacetan jalan di sekitar kampus.

Tepat saat aku terjebak di tengah kepadatan orang-orang yang sedang mencari makan juga, pandanganku teralihkan ke tepi jalan. Di sana, ada pemandangan yang kontras dengan gersangnya aspal.

Beberapa orang sedang berdiri dengan senyum lebar, tangan mereka lincah membagikan tangkai-tangkai bunga gratis kepada setiap pengendara motor yang melambat.

"Kak! Bunga gratis, kak!" salah satu dari mereka memanggil sambil melambaikan tangan ke arahku.

Jujur saja, aku sebenarnya ingin sekali menepi. Ada keinginan impulsif untuk membawa pulang setangkai bunga itu, sekadar untuk jadi penghibur di meja kamar kosku yang berantakan itu, atau sebagai teman membaca buku nanti malam. 

Tapi masalahnya, posisiku benar-benar terkunci di lajur tengah.

“Ah, sudahlah. Nanti deh pas balik lagi,” pikirku menenangkan diri. 

Berbahaya juga kan kalau tiba-tiba memotong jalan hanya demi setangkai bunga.

Singkat cerita, aku sampai di warteg. Membeli seporsi nasi rames dengan berbagai lauk yang lezat. Setelah selesai, aku kembali ke motor dengan perasaan yang lebih tenang dan tentu saja masih ingat soal bunga tadi. Aku sengaja mengambil rute yang sama, sambil membayangkan bakal menyapa kakak-kakak tadi dan menerima setangkai bunga dengan tangan terbuka.

Namun, setibanya di tempat tadi, senyumku perlahan luntur.

Tepi jalan itu sudah sepi. Tidak ada lagi lambaian tangan, tidak ada lagi kakak-kakak dengan keranjang bunga, bahkan tidak ada satu pun helai kelopak bunga yang tertinggal di aspal. Semuanya sudah bersih, seolah-olah pembagian bunga tadi hanya bagian dari mimpi indahku di tengah kemacetan.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was already one of the models that made the DGX Spark interesting.

Now a new optimization is making the single-Spark setup even more compelling.

The reported gains:

Prose decode: +12.5% average
Code decode: +13.7% average

Those percentages might not look huge at first.

But when you’re running a 125B-class MoE model on a single compact machine, a 10%+ throughput improvement is meaningful.

You’re not changing the model.

You’re not waiting for a new GPU generation.

You’re squeezing more performance out of the hardware that’s already sitting there.

That’s the part I find interesting.

The DGX Spark has a very different role from a traditional gaming PC.

It’s designed around running serious AI workloads in a relatively compact form factor, with the software stack doing a lot of the heavy lifting.

And Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a particularly interesting match because it’s a massive MoE model without requiring every parameter to be active for every token.

That means the system doesn’t have to process the entire 125B parameter count at every decoding step.

But getting good real-world performance still requires much more than simply loading the model.

Memory movement matters.

Kernel efficiency matters.

Speculative decoding matters.

Context management matters.

CUDA graph capture matters.

And the inference runtime matters.

That’s why I pay attention when a model gets a double-digit speedup without changing the underlying hardware.

It tells you there was still performance sitting on the table.

A benchmark might say a machine has a certain theoretical capability.

Actual inference often tells a different story.

You can have the same GPU, the same model and the same weights, yet get noticeably different results depending on the implementation.

That’s becoming one of the biggest themes in local AI.

The model is only one layer.

The inference stack is another.

And sometimes the second layer is where the biggest gains are hiding.

For DGX Spark owners, this makes Qwen3.8-Flash-Next even more attractive.

You get a large MoE model with a relatively small active parameter count, and now the single-Spark implementation is reportedly delivering another 12.5% on prose decoding and 13.7% on code decoding on average.

The code number is especially interesting to me.

Coding workloads tend to expose inference bottlenecks quickly because agents generate lots of short responses, inspect files, call tools, receive results and repeat the cycle.

A faster decode path can therefore improve the entire interaction loop.

It isn’t just about watching a token counter climb.

It’s about reducing the time between:

prompt → reasoning → tool call → result → next action.

That’s the metric that matters when you’re actually using an agent.

So if you’re running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on a single DGX Spark, this update is worth paying attention to.

The hardware hasn’t changed.

The model hasn’t suddenly become smaller.

The improvement is coming from the engineering underneath.

And that’s why I think Qwen3.8-Flash-Next remains one of the most interesting models to run on a single Spark.

A 125B-class MoE model on a compact AI system is already impressive.

Getting another 10%+ of practical decoding performance out of the same machine is even more interesting.

That’s the kind of optimization that makes local inference better without asking users to buy another box.

**Sam Altman backs Dario Amodei’s call to “pace the frontier”—and says OpenAI will match Anthropic’s evaluator pledge.**

On September 12, 2026, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman quoted Dario Amodei’s essay *We Must Pace the Frontier* and wrote a short, unusually aligned reply: he agrees the industry needs to slow the rate at which frontier capabilities rise. He added that the subject has been a main topic inside OpenAI in recent weeks. Then came the operational commitment: independent evaluators with employee-like access is “a great idea,” and OpenAI will do the same. More details, he said, would follow.

That is not a minor tweet. For years the public story of frontier AI has been a race—OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, and others shipping larger models, better agents, and more autonomy as fast as compute and data allow. Amodei’s essay argued that the race itself has become the risk. Since summer 2026, he wrote, models have begun helping build the next generation of models. Recursive self-improvement is no longer a thought experiment. Combined with incidents in which agent swarms attacked targets they were not asked to attack, he said the industry should take extra time to align systems, harden operations, and let outsiders verify that safety work is real. Anthropic would go first by giving third-party teams permanent, employee-level access.

Altman’s post accepts that frame. He does not announce a training freeze. He does not endorse every line of Amodei’s three-step plan, which also includes coordination among democratic labs and, eventually, some form of global deal. Base in 2026: Coinbase’s L2 as rails for global onchain finance
Base started as Coinbase’s Ethereum Layer 2 for cheap, fast transactions. By late 2026 it has become one of the busiest settlement layers for stablecoins, tokenized assets, and machine-to-machine payments—not just another scaling chain.5
It is an optimistic rollup that inherits Ethereum security, uses ETH for gas, and keeps fees well under a cent with sub-second feel thanks to Flashblocks. The sequencer is still operated by the Base team, and the network sits at Stage 1 on common rollup frameworks. That trade-off—speed and distribution versus full decentralization—is the live debate around it.1
What stands out now is product density, not slogans.
Stablecoin activity is the clearest signal. Base processes enormous daily transfer volume relative to the supply sitting on the chain. Beyond USDC, local-currency stables have landed: MXNB (Mexican peso via Bitso) and ZARU (South African rand) give remittance and regional settlement corridors a native onchain path. That is how an L2 stops being “crypto-only” and starts looking like payment infrastructure.0
Tokenized equities followed. Coinbase brought 1:1-backed U.S. stock products onto Base using the B20 token standard—real custody, not synthetic wrappers—for assets such as Apple, NVIDIA, Meta, and Alphabet. Eligible users can trade them around the clock. B20 also targets stablecoin issuers and other RWAs with compliance hooks, memos, and metadata that traditional rails already expect.3
AI payments are the newer layer. The x402 standard (named after the old HTTP “Payment Required” code) lets agents pay for APIs and compute in tiny increments. AWS AgentCore Payments plugging into that stack is a concrete example: cloud infrastructure talking to an L2 without a human in the loop. Travala and others have already shipped gasless USDC flows for agentic use cases.0
The consumer surface changed too. The social-first “Base App” experiment underperformed; leadership shifted and the self-custodial product is again Coinbase Wallet, focused on trading, perps, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks. Distribution through Coinbase’s existing user base remains the network’s unfair advantage.7
Technically, Base has been peeling away from a pure OP Stack Superchain identity toward a more unified, Base-operated client and proof mix (TEE plus ZK). Node operators will need to follow that path on future forks. Reliability has been high overall, with isolated sequencer stalls in mid-2026 that the team treated as engineering debt rather than a crisis.8
There is still no official Base network token. Earlier comments about exploring one for governance and sequencer-revenue sharing have not turned into a launch date. Treat any “BASE token” claims as noise unless they come from official channels.
Why it matters in one line: Base is trying to be the default place where dollars, local currencies, stocks, and AI agents settle cheaply on Ethereum security—with Coinbase’s on-ramp sitting next to permissionless DeFi.
Useful starting points: https://t.co/0OBeOTy69z, BaseScan, and the official docs. Always verify contracts and withdrawal paths yourself.

Ada hal menyedihkan yang terus saja berulang dalam program prioritas Makan Bergizi Gratis walau saat ini Kepala BGN sudah berganti, yaitu tentang para guru yang harus mencicipi menu MBG sebelum disantap oleh para murid. Kenapa saya berkata bahwa kebijakan ini tolol? Karena selain bergaji kecil dan tugas yang banyak, guru atau tenaga didik sekarang harus mempertaruhkan kesehatannya sebagai kelinci percobaan. Alih-alih membebankan tugas icip-icip itu ke Quality Control atau Ahli Gizi SPPG, Sudaryono malah menyuruh para guru untuk bertaruh nyawa.

Sebagai manusia yang merdeka, seharusnya Sudaryono mampu untuk berpikir kritis serta objektif, mengingat dirinya mengklaim saat kecil sering memakan telur hingga bisulan guna menunjang perkembangan otaknya. Tapi apa yang terjadi sekarang? Kebijakan yang seharusnya dibebankan ke pihak SPPG malah dibebankan ke guru.

Kebijakan yang dilontarkan Kepala Badan Gizi Nasional itu dibungkus dengan dalih muluk: makan bersama sebagai sarana edukasi tata krama, cuci tangan, berdoa, dan penjelasan kandungan gizi, sekaligus menjadi “pemeriksa organoleptik terakhir.” Artinya, guru diminta melihat, mencium, dan mencicipi makanan. Jika dianggap tidak layak, wajib ditahan dan tidak dibagikan. Di atas kertas terdengar bijak. Di lapangan, ini adalah pengalihan tanggung jawab yang ceroboh.

Sebagai bahan informasi, guru di Indonesia sudah dibebani administrasi berlapis, jam mengajar yang padat, dan tuntutan kurikulum yang terus berubah. Nah, sekarang ditambah peran sebagai penjamin keamanan pangan yang padahal, keamanan pangan adalah domainnya profesional seperti ahli gizi, petugas quality control, dan sistem pengawasan di Satuan Pelayanan Pemenuhan Gizi (SPPG). Kenapa? Karena merekalaj yang dibayar dan dilatih untuk memeriksa suhu, waktu masak, kebersihan, dan potensi kontaminasi. Di sisi lain, guru bukan ahli mikrobiologi, di mana lidah dan hidung mereka tidak dilengkapi alat deteksi bakteri atau toksin. Jika makanan sudah terkontaminasi di dapur, mencicipi hanya akan memindahkan risiko keracunan dari murid ke guru.

Makanan yang dimasak terlalu dini, disimpan melebihi batas aman, atau disiapkan tanpa disiplin higienis adalah yang menjadi sumber masalah. Sehinhga, solusi yang masuk akal adalah dengan memperkuat pengawasan di hulu, misalnya seperti kewajiban uji kimia di setiap SPPG, pemantauan digital waktu masak dan suhu, penandaan batas konsumsi yang ketat pada ompreng, serta sanksi tegas terhadap kepala dapur yang lalai. Sudaryono sendiri memang sudah mencopot ratusan kepala SPPG dan menutup dapur bermasalah, di mana keputusan itu justru menunjukkan bahwa akar masalahnya ada di dapur, bukan di ruang kelas.

Namun alih-alih mempercepat perbaikan sistemik di SPPG, kebijakan ini justru menyerahkan “pemeriksaan terakhir” kepada orang yang paling tidak siap. Mengapa tidak memperkuat peran mereka (SPPG) dengan protokol pemeriksaan profesional, bukan membebani guru? Mengapa tidak memastikan setiap batch makanan melalui uji laboratorium acak atau test kit sederhana sebelum meninggalkan dapur? Mengapa harus menunggu guru menjadi korban pertama?

Kebijakan ini mencerminkan pola pikir yang malas berpikir struktural, di mana ia lebih mudah meminta kesediaan guru “demi edukasi” daripada membangun sistem yang benar-benar bekerja, sehingga dapur bisa disiplin, pengawasan yang ketat berbasis data, dan tenaga ahli yang bertanggung jawab penuh. Hingga usia kemerdekaan yang ke 81 ini, guru sudah cukup berkorban bagi kehidupan bangsa, maka dengan demikian, mereka tidak perlu dijadikan kelinci percobaan atas nama program yang konon demi generasi emas.

Jika Sudaryono benar-benar ingin MBG aman dan bermartabat, ia harus bisa memperbaiki SPPG secara radikal, misalnya dengan merekrut dan melatih lebih banyak ahli gizi, menerapkan uji keamanan yang objektif, bukan organoleptik amatir. Biarkan guru mengajar, jangan paksa mereka bertaruh nyawa hanya karena sistem di dapur masih kacau. Kebijakan yang membebani pihak yang salah, adalah kebijakan tolol. Dan kebijakan tolol, betapa pun dibungkus bahasa edukasi, tetap saja berbahaya bagi orang-orang yang dipaksa melaksanakannya.

Ditulis oleh Hara Nirankara

AGNTS by tut™: When a $5 PFP Becomes an AI Agent, Wallet and Fee Claim

The floor is already around $50
But the most interesting trade is not the JPEG

------------------
Phase 1 of tut™ (@Tuteth_) AGNTS is complete.
The launch was originally scheduled for September 10, then delayed after the team found bugs during the community round. The mint has now finished, secondary trading is live on OpenSea, and the collection is verified on Robinhood Chain.

At the time I checked, the floor was around $50.

That is roughly 5x the $10 normal wallet mint price and more than 10x the roughly $5 price available through an AGNT wallet.

Nice start.

But I think the floor is almost the least interesting part of this launch.

Tut is trying to turn a PFP into something much stranger: an AI agent identity, smart wallet, liquidity instrument and claim on activity generated by the platform around it 👇

🔹This Is (by far) Not Tut’s First NFT Experiment🔹

Tut did not appear last week with an AI wrapper and a mint page.

He has been shipping digital art collections before AGNT, including Abstractions on Abstract and Legend of Breadio on MegaETH, then using those collectors as the early community around AGNT.

That history matters because AGNT itself is already a working product rather than a roadmap screenshot. 
Its trading interface is live across multiple chains, and the product combines an agent profile, wallet, chat and onchain execution. 
AGNT (@AGNTSOCIAL) is not yet working as well as Grok bot or Hermes but it is specialized on on-chain activities and always improving

The PFP is the attempt to connect that product to an owned identity layer.

That gives this launch a different question from most NFT drops: can an existing collector community become the ownership and distribution layer for an agentic product?

🔹The Supply Number Is More Complicated Than 6,969🔹

The project describes 6,969 fully onchain ERC721C NFTs, hand drawn by tut.

But only about half were designed for the initial community mint. Project materials put roughly 3,434 in the mint and 3,535 inside the tut AMM vault for liquidity, rerolls and swaps.

Those are very different economic buckets.

The vault inventory is not the same thing as current liquid float, but it can become available through the system. And the advertised path toward roughly 1,400 circulating AGNTs depends on holders actually using the burn ladder:

- 5 Commons → 1 Rare
- 3 Rares → 1 Epic
- 2 Epics → 1 Legendary

So 1,400 is a design destination, not today’s supply and not a guaranteed endpoint.

👉 Maximum supply, vault inventory and economic float should never be treated as the same number.

🔹The Burn Math Is Smarter Than It Looks🔹

This is the part I find most elegant.
Published reward weights are:

- Common = 1x
- Rare = 5x
- Epic = 15x
- Legendary = 30x

Now compare them with the burn recipe.

- 5 Commons carry 5 units of reward weight and become 1 Rare carrying 5.
- 3 Rares carry 15 and become 1 Epic carrying 15.
- 2 Epics carry 30 and become 1 Legendary carrying 30.

The burn therefore appears almost perfectly weight neutral for fee sharing.

👉 Burning compresses claims, it does not magically manufacture more reward weight.

That matters enormously for valuation.
A Rare should not automatically be worth more than five Commons merely because it is rarer. 

The premium has to come from art, liquidity, convenience, future tier privileges or some other benefit beyond the published fee multiplier.

The same logic applies all the way up the ladder.
This creates an actual arbitrage framework rather than a vague scarcity story.

🔹Then The PFP Starts Looking Like Financial Infrastructure🔹

The next phase is where the experiment becomes more ambitious.

Each PFP is designed to have an ERC6551 bound wallet, an onchain persona and the ability to operate inside AGNT. In the live interface, holders can already interact with their AGNT from chat to buy, sell, bid or send.

Activation is supposed to turn the NFT into an active protocol participant.

Project materials describe a system where active AGNTs receive 70% of several platform fee streams, weighted by rarity, while the treasury receives 30%.

The design also includes secondary and vault fees, curated launch fees, activation fees and planned RWA distributions directly into the NFT bound wallet.

That makes the PFP less like a profile picture and more like a programmable account with economic rights attached to its activity.

But the word everyone will be tempted to use is yield.

I would use a different word for now: claim.

The platform has reported 16K active wallets, more than $6M of volume and more than $60K of revenue, but those figures are team reported and the relevant time windows and distributable fee base matter enormously.

A 70% share of a small fee pool is still a small fee pool.

🔹$AGNTS Is The Next Test🔹

The planned $AGNTS token is supposed to connect the PFP to the liquidity layer.

The published design describes 1B tokens, with 50% allocated to a fair launch and 50% to the AMM vault backing PFP redemption values.

The proposed tier values are 100K $AGNTS for a Common, 500K for a Rare, 1.5M for an Epic and 3M for a Legendary. 
Activation is supposed to burn 50% of the associated token value while making the NFT eligible for rewards.

🔄 That creates two linked scarcity loops: NFT consolidation through burns, and token destruction through activation.

But this is also where I become more cautious.

At the time of writing I have not independently verified a live official $AGNTS contract. There is already an older token called AGNT SOCIAL on Base, and it is not the same instrument.

👉 Until the official $AGNTS contract is published through verified AGNT channels, ticker search is not due diligence.

🔹Is The $50 Floor Still Attractive?🔹

This is where mint economics and secondary economics separate completely.

At $5 or $10, the initial decision was tiny optionality on a builder with an existing product, an art history and a complex incentive system still ahead of it.

Around $50, you are paying five to ten times more before the token, burn market, gacha system and fee distributions have established real price discovery.

That does not make the secondary expensive by definition.
It means the thesis now needs operating evidence.

I would watch actual protocol fees, active AGNTs, vault liquidity, $AGNTS depth, burn participation and whether curated launches create recurring volume rather than one launch week spike.

The architecture is interesting.
The cash flow still has to earn the floor.

🔹What I Would Actually Do🔹

▫️ If I minted cheaply, I would preserve optionality through Phase 2 rather than rushing into every mechanic on day one.

📝 Wait for burns, rerolls and the official $AGNTS contract to be live, then compare what each action gives up against what it unlocks before activating or burning.

▫️ I would treat each rarity conversion as an exchange rate, not a gamified upgrade.

📝 Compare Rare floor versus 5 Commons, Epic versus 3 Rares and Legendary versus 2 Epics before burning. 
If the higher tier trades below the input basket, buying it directly can be economically cleaner.

▫️ I would not extrapolate the roughly $53 floor into a yield thesis yet.

📝 Track protocol fee revenue per day and the amount actually distributed to active AGNTs. 
That is the operating variable that can eventually justify a financial premium over the art.

▫️ For a fresh secondary buyer, I would size this very differently from the mint.

📝 Treat the current entry as a speculative satellite whose plausible loss is most of the purchase price. 
The $5 asymmetric mint is gone; the secondary buyer needs execution evidence now.

▫️ I would be extremely careful around the token launch.

📝 Use only the contract published through verified AGNT or tut channels and confirm chain, supply and vault mechanics before trading. 
Do not confuse $AGNTS with the older AGNT SOCIAL token on Base.

▫️ My falsifier is operating demand, not the floor chart.

📝 If wallet activity, recurring fee revenue, curated launch volume and actual distributions fail to grow after the token and burn systems go live, then scarcity is mostly circulating among existing collectors rather than being paid for by a growing protocol.

The NFT market right now is all about adding utility to JPEGs.

AGNTS is trying the reverse: start with an operating agent platform, then make the JPEG its identity and economic shell.

The burn therefore appears almost perfectly weight neutral for fee sharing. 👉 Burning compresses claims, it does not magically manufacture more reward weight. That matters enormously for valuation. A Rare should not automatically be worth more than five Commons merely because it is rarer. The premium has to come from art, liquidity, convenience, future tier privileges or some other benefit beyond the published fee multiplier. The same logic applies all the way up the ladder. This creates an actual arbitrage framework rather than a vague scarcity story. 🔹Then The PFP Starts Looking Like Financial Infrastructure🔹 The next phase is where the experiment becomes more ambitious. Each PFP is designed to have an ERC6551 bound wallet, an onchain persona and the ability to operate inside AGNT. In the live interface, holders can already interact with their AGNT from chat to buy, sell, bid or send. Activation is supposed to turn the NFT into an active protocol participant. Project materials describe a system where active AGNTs receive 70% of several platform fee streams, weighted by rarity, while the treasury receives 30%. The design also includes secondary and vault fees, curated launch fees, activation fees and planned RWA distributions directly into the NFT bound wallet. That makes the PFP less like a profile picture and more like a programmable account with economic rights attached to its activity. But the word everyone will be tempted to use is yield. I would use a different word for now: claim. The platform has reported 16K active wallets, more than $6M of volume and more than $60K of revenue, but those figures are team reported and the relevant time windows and distributable fee base matter enormously. A 70% share of a small fee pool is still a small fee pool. 🔹$AGNTS Is The Next Test🔹 The planned $AGNTS token is supposed to connect the PFP to the liquidity layer. The published design describes 1B tokens, with 50% allocated to a fair launch and 50% to the AMM vault backing PFP redemption values. The proposed tier values are 100K $AGNTS for a Common, 500K for a Rare, 1.5M for an Epic and 3M for a Legendary. Activation is supposed to burn 50% of the associated token value while making the NFT eligible for rewards. 🔄 That creates two linked scarcity loops: NFT consolidation through burns, and token destruction through activation. But this is also where I become more cautious. At the time of writing I have not independently verified a live official $AGNTS contract. There is already an older token called AGNT SOCIAL on Base, and it is not the same instrument. 👉 Until the official $AGNTS contract is published through verified AGNT channels, ticker search is not due diligence. 🔹Is The $50 Floor Still Attractive?🔹 This is where mint economics and secondary economics separate completely. At $5 or $10, the initial decision was tiny optionality on a builder with an existing product, an art history and a complex incentive system still ahead of it. Around $50, you are paying five to ten times more before the token, burn market, gacha system and fee distributions have established real price discovery. That does not make the secondary expensive by definition. It means the thesis now needs operating evidence. I would watch actual protocol fees, active AGNTs, vault liquidity, $AGNTS depth, burn participation and whether curated launches create recurring volume rather than one launch week spike. The architecture is interesting. The cash flow still has to earn the floor. 🔹What I Would Actually Do🔹 ▫️ If I minted cheaply, I would preserve optionality through Phase 2 rather than rushing into every mechanic on day one. 📝 Wait for burns, rerolls and the official $AGNTS contract to be live, then compare what each action gives up against what it unlocks before activating or burning. ▫️ I would treat each rarity conversion as an exchange rate, not a gamified upgrade. 📝 Compare Rare floor versus 5 Commons, Epic versus 3 Rares and Legendary versus 2 Epics before burning. If the higher tier trades below the input basket, buying it directly can be economically cleaner. ▫️ I would not extrapolate the roughly $53 floor into a yield thesis yet. 📝 Track protocol fee revenue per day and the amount actually distributed to active AGNTs. That is the operating variable that can eventually justify a financial premium over the art. ▫️ For a fresh secondary buyer, I would size this very differently from the mint. 📝 Treat the current entry as a speculative satellite whose plausible loss is most of the purchase price. The $5 asymmetric mint is gone; the secondary buyer needs execution evidence now. ▫️ I would be extremely careful around the token launch. 📝 Use only the contract published through verified AGNT or tut channels and confirm chain, supply and vault mechanics before trading. Do not confuse $AGNTS with the older AGNT SOCIAL token on Base. ▫️ My falsifier is operating demand, not the floor chart. 📝 If wallet activity, recurring fee revenue, curated launch volume and actual distributions fail to grow after the token and burn systems go live, then scarcity is mostly circulating among existing collectors rather than being paid for by a growing protocol. The NFT market right now is all about adding utility to JPEGs. AGNTS is trying the reverse: start with an operating agent platform, then make the JPEG its identity and economic shell.

• Low-setup self-hosting – run it with Bun and embedded PGlite, with optional integrations degrading gracefully until configured

It’s open-source (AGPL-3.0 license).

text:
Browser agents get useful when they can read a page and do the next step.

WebBrain is an open-source browser extension that puts an AI agent in a side panel for people who want to chat with pages, automate browser tasks, and run multi-step workflows.

It helps you move from a question or browser task to controlled execution by separating read-only Ask, action-oriented Act, and Dev modes.

Key features:

• Page reading – reads text, links, forms, tables, PDFs, and interactive elements through the accessibility tree
• Controlled actions – can click, type, scroll, navigate, upload, download, and verify forms, with per-site permission prompts before consequential actions
• Plan before action – Act and Dev can generate a structured plan for approval before running tools
• Model choice – supports local servers such as llama.cpp and Ollama, plus cloud APIs
• Reusable automation – successful runs can become saved workflows, with scheduled tasks and page watches available

It’s open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later license).

Link in the reply 👇

text:
A 9B reasoning model that runs locally on a phone just got an uncensored build.

And this one is more interesting than the usual “small local LLM” release: the original Ornith-1.5-9B was specifically built for reasoning, coding and agentic workloads, with an official mobile variant for iPhone and Android. 

Now community developers have released abliterated / uncensored GGUF versions, removing much of the model's refusal behavior while keeping it compatible with local runtimes. 

The numbers are surprisingly good for something this small.

Ornith-1.5-9B scores 70.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 47.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. According to the Ornith team, that puts the 9B model around or above significantly larger open models like Gemma 4-31B and Qwen 3.6-35B on some agentic coding evaluations. 

You also get:

➖ 262,144-token native context
➖ built-in reasoning mode
➖ native tool calling for AI agents
➖ OpenAI-compatible serving
➖ local inference through llama.cpp / Ollama
➖ GGUF quantizations small enough for consumer hardware

A Q4 build of one uncensored release is only ~5.6 GB, while Q6 is ~7.4 GB. That makes running it on machines with roughly 8 GB of available memory plausible, although your usable context will be much smaller than the theoretical 256K at that memory budget. 

There's one important catch with the specific GGUF builds: don't assume you're getting the full multimodal Ornith experience. Some uncensored GGUF releases contain only the text model and omit the vision projector, even though the original base model is multimodal. 

The more interesting story here isn't really “uncensored AI.”

We're getting to the point where a model small enough to carry around locally can reason, write code, call tools and act as the brain of an agent without sending every prompt to OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.
And unlike a cloud model, your prompts and files can stay entirely on your own device.

text:
A 27B model running in full BF16 on free Kaggle TPU compute is probably not where most people expected local AI to go.

But that’s exactly what makes this interesting.

Qwen3.8-27B is reportedly running on a Kaggle TPU v5e-8 at roughly:

130 tok/s decode
10,000 tok/s prefill
262K context

And this isn’t a heavily compressed version of the model.

No Q4. No Q3.

No aggressive quantization just to squeeze the weights into a consumer GPU.

It’s running in BF16.

The 10,000 tok/s prefill figure is probably the number I’d pay the most attention to.

Generation speed gets all the attention because it’s easy to understand.

But for coding agents, document analysis and long-context workloads, prompt processing can become a major part of the experience.

Imagine handing the model a large repository, a huge stack of documentation, tool outputs and a long conversation.

If the system can ingest that information extremely quickly, the model can get to the actual reasoning stage much sooner.

Then you’re still getting around 130 tokens per second during generation.

That’s a pretty unusual combination.

But the hardware numbers aren’t even the most interesting part.

The model can reportedly be exposed through an OpenAI-compatible API.

That changes the experiment completely.

Instead of building an entirely new application around the TPU setup, you can point software that already understands OpenAI-style endpoints at it.

That opens the door to coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other compatible clients.

The workflow becomes surprisingly straightforward.

Start the Qwen3.8-27B instance.

Expose the model through an API endpoint.

Configure your coding client to use that endpoint.

Now your existing agent workflow can talk to an open-weight 27B model running on the backend.

No custom interface. No rebuilding your entire tooling stack. And then there’s the context window.

262K tokens is enormous for agentic coding.

A large repository can stay in context for much longer.

Tool outputs have more room.

Long debugging sessions don’t have to be constantly compressed.

Documentation, source files, test results and previous reasoning can coexist without immediately hitting the context ceiling.

That matters because context is becoming one of the hidden costs of AI coding.

A model might be extremely capable, but if your agent keeps throwing away information every few turns because the context window is too small, you lose a lot of that capability.

A 262K context gives the agent much more room to work.

And the fact that this is being demonstrated on a free Kaggle TPU is the part that really changes the economics.

You don’t necessarily need a $2,000 GPU sitting under your desk.

You don’t necessarily need an expensive dedicated cloud instance.

You can combine free accelerator access with open weights and an API layer that existing developer tools already understand.

That creates a very different path to experimenting with serious models.

Open models are becoming easier to access.

Accelerator software is getting better.

Inference servers are becoming more compatible.

And coding agents don’t particularly care whether the model behind the endpoint lives on your RTX card, a TPU or somewhere in the cloud.

They just need an API that works.

That’s the bigger story here.

The interesting question isn’t simply whether Qwen3.8-27B can hit 130 tok/s.

It’s whether open models plus cheap or free compute can become a practical alternative backend for the tools developers already use every day.

If that continues improving, the barrier to experimenting with large open models gets dramatically lower.

The model is open. The weights are available. The interface is familiar.

And in this case, the accelerator doesn’t even have to be yours.

That’s a pretty wild direction for AI infrastructure.

MBG DALAM SOROTAN PUBLIK

Sebelum Kepala Badan Gizi Nasional, Dadan Hindayana, dan dua wakilnya ditahan kejaksaan untuk kasus korupsi pengelolaan Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), kecurigaan publik bahwa program ini tidak dikelola secara bersih dan profesional sudah besar dan memicu ketidakpuasan pada pelaksanaanya. Pada November 2025, angka kepuasan publik pada pelaksanaan program unggulan Prabowo ini masih sekitar 62,5 persen. Angka ini menurun menjadi 53,1 persen pada awal Maret 2026. Setelah itu, angkanya merosot semakin drastis menjadi hanya 33,8 persen. 

Sebaliknya, yang mengaku tidak puas naik dari 33,9 menjadi 44,6 dan terus meroket mencapai 61,6 persen. 

Ini ironis karena program yang justru paling diandalkan oleh pemerintah itu justru semakin hari semakin tidak populer di kalangan warga pada umumnya. Iming-iming bergizi dan gratis tidak membuat warga terkecoh dan kehilangan daya kritis. Mereka mengamati secara detil pelaksanaan program yang awalnya bernama makan siang gratis itu. 

Warga pada dasarnya sadar bahwa sebenarnya tidak ada makan siang gratis. Program itu mengambil alokasi anggaran pendidikan, mengambil jatah pembangunan infrastruktur penting, menggerogoti dana pembangunan pemerintahan daerah, memperkecil dana layanan publik pelbagai kementerian, dan lain-lain. 

Dalam pengalaman sejak hari pertama diterapkan, publik sudah terinformasi bahwa program ini juga tidak sepenuhnya bergizi. Ribuan siswa justru keracunan setelah menyantap makanan yang diolah secara terpusat di luar sekolah itu. Belum lagi banyak kasus makanan yang basi ketika sampai ke sekolah. 

Persoalan ini menjadi lebih rumit oleh kasus korupsi yang sudah menjerat direksi BGN dan tidak menutup kemungkinan hal yang sama terjadi sampai ke level bawah. Inkonsistensi penganggaran dari 335 triliun menjadi 268 dan sekarang 229 triliun menunjukkan program ini dilakukan secara tidak serius berdasarkan kajian yang memadai. Dan ini terjadi sejak awal di mana target persoalan yang ingin diselesaikan adalah stunting tapi berujung menjadi program makan bagi semua dengan jumlah besar, sekitar 82 juta kepala. 

Program dengan dana besar di tengah budaya korupsi dan minimnya pengawasan legislatif membuat publik kehilangan kepercayaan. Dan itu bukan sesuatu yang mengejutkan. 

Jakarta, 28 Juli 2026
SAIDIMAN AHMAD

Coding agents move fast. Reviewing their work shouldn’t mean chasing tabs and diffs.

Nimbalyst is an open-source visual workspace for builders working with Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and other coding agents.

It helps you keep agent sessions, worktrees, tasks, and the files they touch in one place by pairing visual editors with session management and built-in Git workflows.

Key features:

• Visual editors – edit markdown, mockups, diagrams, CSVs, data models, and code alongside an agent
• Red/green diff review – step through proposed edits in rendered documents and accept or reject each change
• Parallel agent sessions – run several agents at once, each isolated in its own Git worktree
• Session kanban – track, search, resume, and link sessions to the files they touched
• Plain files on disk – keep content and workflow status in your Git repo rather than a proprietary store

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Terima kasih untuk Kepala SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek yang Mengkritik MBG

Oleh: Hariqo Satria*

Guru kita Kepala SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek, Bapak Ikhsan Nur Wahyudi mengatakan:

SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek memutuskan tidak lagi ikut program Makan Bergizi Gratis atau MBG.

Beliau menyampaikan tiga penyebabnya:

Pertama, MBG itu menyita waktu pelajaran minimal setengah jam, atau mengurangi durasi pembelajaran.

Kedua, SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek merasa ada sekolah yang lebih membutuhkan.

Ketiga, masalah sisa makanan yang mubazir.

Beliau melanjutkan seperti yang ditulis beberapa media, keputusan tersebut bukan karena sekolah menolak pentingnya pemenuhan gizi bagi anak-anak.

Karena itu, sekolah memilih kembali mengoptimalkan program makan siang mandiri yang telah dijalankan sejak awal berdiri.

Terima kasih kami haturkan kepada yang kami hormati Kepala SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek, Bapak Ikhsan Nur Wahyudi.

Kami sangat menghormati. Pernyataan Bapak Ikhsan Nur Wahyudi di poin kedua dan ketiga itu benar, di bagian bawah kami apresiasi dan jelaskan.

Baik, yang pertama soal jam pelajaran.

Dengan hormat perlu kami sampaikan bahwa MBG itu sendiri adalah pelajaran.

Sebelum, saat atau sesudah makan adalah saat yang tepat untuk menyampaikan tentang:

1) Penghormatan terhadap perjuangan dari Ibu Bapak kita para petani, peternak, nelayan, pekebun, dan pengusaha lokal yang menyediakan bahan pangan kita.

2) Penumbuhan rasa hormat atas perjuangan para guru, tenaga kesehatan dalam mengedukasi soal gizi, dan perjuangan kedua orang tua siswa di rumah yang berjuang menafkahi keluarga.

3) Pendidikan gizi terapan untuk membangun pola makan seimbang dan mencegah masalah kesehatan, seperti anemia, cuci darah sejak usia dini.

4) Penerapan tata krama makan serta penumbuhan kesadaran untuk tidak menyisakan makanan, menceritakan cara mengolah limbah.

5) Pengenalan dasar konsep kemandirian dan swasembada pangan nasional.

6) Edukasi mengenai kekayaan dan keberagaman komoditas pangan lokal Nusantara. Menjelaskan Bhinneka Tunggal Ika dari makanan.

7) Pemberian ruang ekspresi bagi siswa untuk secara bergantian menceritakan tradisi atau budaya makan di keluarga masing-masing.

8) Pendidikan karakter praktis melalui budaya antre, gotong royong saat menyajikan makanan, hingga tanggung jawab merapikan peralatan makan sendiri.

9) Wawasan global mengenai proses perjalanan program "MBG" di berbagai negara yang telah berjalan selama 50 tahun bahkan di atas 70 tahun.

10) Penanaman nilai-nilai integritas, transparansi, dan kejujuran sebagai dasar pencegahan korupsi sejak usia dini.

Tentu saja, pendidikan ini bisa kita sisipkan secara alami dan bertahap, bukan diubah menjadi mata pelajaran formal baru yang membebani Ibu dan Bapak kita para guru.

Hal Ini sepenuhnya menyesuaikan dengan kebijaksanaan dan kenyamanan sekolah, dan memang ada penelitian yang menyebutkan bahwa makan bersama itu sehat.

Di Jepang, makan siang di sekolah dikenal dengan istilah Kyushoku dianggap sebagai bagian dari pendidikan moral dan karakter.

Siswa diajarkan tentang kesetaraan, rasa hormat dan tanggung jawab soal kebersihan karena tidak ada staf kebersihan, menumbuhkan rasa syukur dan kebanggaan pada pangan lokal.

Intinya makan di sekolah adalah media praktis untuk mengajarkan kerja sama tim, empati, dan tanggung jawab sosial.

MBG di Indonesia itu mirip di Jepang dengan sistem dapur umum atau SPPG.

Nanti di daerah 3T akan berkolaborasi dengan sekolah, beserta penyesuaian lainnya. Kritik dan saran dari siapa pun sangat-sangat berharga.

Kedua, kami setuju dengan Kepala SD Muhammadiyah 1 Trenggalek, Bapak Ikhsan Nur Wahyudi.

Kita memahami bahwa setiap sekolah memiliki situasi yg berbeda.

Jika sebuah sekolah telah memiliki fasilitas atau program internal yg memadai untuk memenuhi standar gizi siswanya, serta didukung kemampuan partisipasi para orang tua dan kemandirian gizi dari pihak keluarga, maka sekolah tersebut memiliki hak untuk tidak ikut serta dalam program MBG.

Three competing payment giants just admitted their closed protocols don't work alone.

Visa, Mastercard and Ant International each built their own separate system for verifying AI shopping agents, and none of them talked to each other.

This week they announced a shared Know-Your-Agent framework, so an agent verified on one network doesn't need to re-register on the others.

Ant's piece of this, the Agentic Mobile Protocol, has been open source since April.

It took three trillion dollars of projected agentic commerce hitting a wall before the closed players agreed to open up.

Interoperability is rarely a closed platform's first move. It's what happens after the closed approach stops scaling.

IEEE Spectrum published some remarkable numbers:

42% of code entering shared codebases is already estimated to be AI-assisted or generated.

Yet 96% of developers don’t fully trust AI output to work correctly.

At one company, code entering review increased 10×. Review time tripled.

Now look at your own software delivery process.

What would happen if your teams produced 10× more code tomorrow?

Could requirements keep up?
Could testing? Security? Architecture? Release?

Or would you simply create a much bigger queue?

This is why I’m skeptical when companies target “70% developer productivity” or “50% faster coding.”

They are optimizing one step of a system.

Let agents write and review most of the code. Move humans upstream into specification and downstream into judgment.

Amazon provides a fascinating example.

An incomplete specification caused an agent to generate 25,000 lines of code in the wrong Swift version.

They fixed the specification.
The agent regenerated the solution in about 15 minutes.

The scarce resource wasn’t coding.

So perhaps we are measuring AI coding productivity wrong.

Start asking:

The escalating AI race has triggered a wave of high-profile resignations across leading labs. Key researchers are leaving not to join competitors, but to sound the alarm on how commercial pressures are systematically overriding safety protocols.

OpenAI: The Dissolution of the Superalignment Team
The most prominent departures occurred when Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike, co-leads of the Superalignment team (tasked with steering superintelligent AI), resigned. Shortly after, OpenAI dissolved the entire team.
Whistleblower Voice: Upon resigning, Jan Leike publicly stated:"Over the past years, safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products... OpenAI must become a safety-first AGI company."  
The Consequences: The dissolution of the team tasked with preventing catastrophic AI risks highlighted a structural shift: safety research is treated as an impediment to rapid deployment.

Anthropic: The Dilemma of "Safety-Focused" Labs
Anthropic was originally founded by former OpenAI researchers who left over safety concerns. However, the pressure to match Google and OpenAI in model capabilities has forced Anthropic into the same competitive trap.
Whistleblower Voice: Mrinank Sharma, who led Anthropic's Safeguards Team, announced his departure with a stark warning:"I am leaving because the speed of deployment is outpacing our collective capacity to understand and control these systems safely."  
The Consequences: Even companies explicitly built on alignment research are compressing evaluation timelines for autonomous agents to maintain market relevance, shortening the window to catch critical vulnerabilities.

Meta & Google DeepMind: Market Speed vs. Risk Mitigation
At legacy tech giants, internal ethical oversight has repeatedly clashed with product timelines. Meta’s open-source strategy for its Llama models and Google’s rush to deploy Gemini-class systems have driven internal dissent.
Whistleblower Voice: Former DeepMind and Meta safety researchers, speaking to major media outlets following their resignations, described an environment where rigorous red-teaming was truncated:"We were being asked to evaluate model safety in weeks rather than months. Leadership didn't want to hear 'no'; they wanted to know when we could hit launch."  
The Consequences: Releasing highly capable, unaligned open-source models or pushing agentic AI to production without adequate containment significantly lowers the barrier for bad actors to automate cyberattacks, generate biological risk vectors, or weaponize synthetic media at scale.

HSBC: Competition from Chinese models is serious but isn't likely to impact overall AI spending 

 On top of it, token price is falling significantly and Jevon's paradox is in full flow. 

- Token prices are down significantly but token volume has increased 3x since June
-  OpenRouter ran a discount experiment by offering discount to OpenAI's Terra and Luna models.
- Usage during discount was 5.6x and 13.8x vs 1.1x when it undiscounted. 32% of user continued using even without discounts.
- Chinese models may have captured 50+% token volume but Anthropic and Open still take up ~80% of token spend since 2025 (data source: Vercel)
- Price per token is becoming less important than cost per task. Multiplying volume of workload drives this. 
- Open AI Astra model is 6.5x cost of Kimi3 but cost per task is only 2x higher than Kimi3.
- Agentic application requires higher token consumption & more supervision increasing the token need. Reliability commands premium. 
- Chinese models' current pricing are already proving to be unsustainable. Price increases are underway.
- Hyperscalers likely to earn even if enterprises adopt open source models.
- Expecting both open and closed models would co-exist. 

HSBC concludes that US frontier models would be used complex reasoning & Chinese models would be used for high volume price sensitive workloads.

Sounds a lot like the early days of manufacturing offshoring, doesn't it?

⚠️Viral, Biro Pers Istana Cabut ID Card Jurnalis CNN Indonesia Karena Bertanya Soal MBG⚠️

ID Card jurnalis CNN Indonesia, Diana Valencia, dicabut oleh Biro Pers Istana Kepresidenan. Penyebabnya, Diana bertanya kepada Presiden Prabowo Subianto soal masalah dalam program makan bergizi gratis (MBG) yang dianggap di luar konteks acara.

“Selamat malam, kakak-kakak. Per (Sabtu, 27/9) malam ini, saya bukan wartawan Istana lagi karena ID Card saya sudah diambil oleh Biro Pers,” tulis Diana di pesan WhatsApp yang tangkapan layarnya viral di media sosial.

Dikutip Tempo, sejumlah narasumber yang mengetahui peristiwa tersebut bercerita bahwa Biro Pers, Media, dan Informasi Sekretariat Presiden melarang wartawan Istana menanyakan persoalan selain kunjungan Prabowo.

Prabowo menjelaskan soal pertemuannya dengan sejumlah kepala negara dalam sidang Majelis Umum Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa.

Seorang reporter CNN Indonesia bertanya apakah Prabowo memberi instruksi khusus kepada Badan Gizi Nasional (BGN) soal MBG. Belakangan, kasus keracunan MBG meluas di berbagai daerah.

Prabowo menjawab bahwa ia akan memanggil Kepala BGN Dadan Hindayana. “Saya memonitor perkembangan itu. Habis ini, saya akan panggil langsung Kepala BGN dan beberapa pejabat,” kata Prabowo.

Sejumlah narasumber mengatakan bahwa Biro Pers, Media, dan Informasi Sekretariat Presiden memanggil reporter CNN Indonesia itu, menyatakan berkeberatan atas pertanyaan itu kepada Presiden. Mereka menilai pertanyaan itu di luar konteks.

Setelah itu, Biro Pers mencabut kartu liputan istana milik reporter tersebut. 

Kartu liputan Istana diberikan hanya kepada wartawan tertentu yang memenuhi sejumlah syarat. Tanpa kartu tersebut, wartawan tak bisa masuk ke dalam Istana.

Your coding agent shouldn’t edit before it understands the codebase.

Empirica is an AI measurement framework for builders using AI coding agents across sessions.

It helps you make agent work more grounded by requiring investigation before edits, preserving findings between sessions, and measuring confidence against checks.

Key features:

• Sentinel gate – blocks code edits until the agent demonstrates understanding
• Four-layer memory – keeps findings, unknowns, dead ends, and decisions across sessions
• Calibration model – compares self-assessment, deterministic checks, and grounded reasoning
• Live statusline – surfaces confidence, thresholds, open goals, and work state in the terminal
• Codebase tracking – extracts functions, classes, and imports from file edits to track what is current

It’s open-source (MIT license).

Reflection on Muse & Meta (and I may sold stocks a bit earlier than I should)

Ugh, even though I'm bearish on Meta long-term, I should have anticipated that Muse Spark was something Meta was capable of building, and that I should have waited for it to actually launch before selling.

My mistakes were as follows:
1- Meta is under strong pressure to produce something that excites the stock price in the AI era. So regardless of how things ultimately turn out, this type of product was bound to launch.
2- Meta's rec systems are very strong, and agent memory/context is fundamentally a rec system problem.
3- Meta now has enough money, compute, and data centers to roll out free VMs and agents at scale to a much larger user base. And Meta built its whole business on the application layer, so its infra should be excellent. It's a reasonable inference that they could conceive of and build an agent that's usable and performant.
4- Meta still has a fairly strong network effect - you can see this from how it cold-started Threads off the back of Instagram.

That said, reflection aside, I don't actually have much confidence that Meta can operate the Muse agent well over the long run. I think the personal AI assistant business itself is already highly controversial on ethical and privacy grounds. At the very least, the general public in the US is still quite opposed to consumer-facing AI, and if it's Meta doing it, that could compound the problem even further. That's not to say I trust Instinct (or any competitor) more either - obviously you can't burn cash offering this for free forever.

Of course, I myself am still a fairly committed former-Poke, current-Instinct user!
